# last-price-workspace-admin: tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync.mjs from the live tools/list. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every tool below is on the Last Price MCP server (`https://api.last-price.ai/api/mcp/rpc?profile=directory`).
A tool missing from your own `tools/list` is not switched on for your connection yet.

## `mint_child_key`

Create a short-lived child key for a sub-agent or job, returned only once. Ask for 1 to 20 concrete scopes within your current grants; no wildcards or administration scopes. The default lifetime is five minutes; request 60 to 86400 seconds, capped by your key, token and ancestors. The child stays in this workspace with the same agent binding and quotas. Revoking or rotating an ancestor stops its descendants. Needs an API key or a current token exchanged from one; no human step. Keep the returned key secret.

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/api-keys/children`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `name` | string |  |
| `scopes` **(required)** | array |  |
| `expires_in_seconds` | integer |  |

## `revoke_child_key`

Revoke a direct child of the key this connection uses, by its key id. The child and its descendants stop working. You cannot revoke another parent's child or an unrelated workspace key. Needs an API key or a current token exchanged from one.

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** **destructive**
- **REST:** `/api/api-keys/children/{keyId}`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `key_id` **(required)** | string |  |

## `archive_notifications`

Archive notifications for this reader only (your agent, or your key): pass ids, each an item id as list_notifications returns it (at most 100), or all: true to archive everything created up to archive_through (default now). An archived item leaves your list and never counts as unread; list_notifications with view archived shows it, and unarchive_notifications moves it back. Ids that are not in your feed are listed as not found. Answers 404 (not released) until notification archive is switched on for your workspace. Needs a Last Price credential with notifications write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, notifications write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **Errors and cautions:** Answers 404 (not released) until notification archive is switched on for your workspace.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `ids` | array | Notification ids, as list_notifications returns them (such as approval:<uuid>). |
| `all` | boolean | true archives every item created up to archive_through. Send ids or all, not both. |
| `archive_through` | string | With all: archive everything created at or before this time, ISO 8601. Defaults to now. |

## `unarchive_notifications`

Move archived notifications back to your list, for this reader only: pass ids (at most 100), as list_notifications with view archived returns them. Works for an item that archive all covered too; the rest stays archived. Answers 404 (not released) until notification archive is switched on for your workspace. Needs a Last Price credential with notifications write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, notifications write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **Errors and cautions:** Answers 404 (not released) until notification archive is switched on for your workspace.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `ids` **(required)** | array | Notification ids, as list_notifications returns them (such as approval:<uuid>). |

## `create_workspace`

Create a new workspace (with its sandbox), owned by the person who created your key, on the free plan. Needs an API key sent as x-api-key that holds the workspace:admin scope, made by someone who is still an owner or admin of the workspace; a token or any other key is refused. Where workspace administration by key is not released for your workspace the call is refused with 403. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **Errors and cautions:** Needs an API key sent as x-api-key that holds the workspace:admin scope, made by someone who is still an owner or admin of the workspace; a token or any other key is refused. Where workspace administration by key is not released for your workspace the call is refused with 403.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `name` **(required)** | string | The workspace name. |
| `email` **(required)** | string | Contact email for the workspace. |
| `slug` | string | URL-safe slug (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). Made from the name when left out. |
| `mode` | `managed` / `byok` | managed (default) or byok. |

## `create_child_workspace`

Create a child agent workspace under your own: an unclaimed sandbox with its own agent, key and one-time claim link, for a sub-agent or a separate piece of work. The answer carries the child's key (shown once) and its claim link. When a person claims your workspace, unclaimed children come with it; a child can also be claimed on its own and stays under yours. Needs an agent's credential of a workspace an agent registered (claimed or not), at most 10 children by default, and is off until child agent workspaces are switched on for your workspace.

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `name` **(required)** | string | The child agent's name: letters, digits, spaces and . _ : @ / + -, starting with a letter or digit. |
| `intended_use` | string | What the child is for, shown to the person who claims it. |

## `list_child_workspaces`

List the agent workspaces under yours, newest first: the children your agents created and the agent workspaces claimed into it, each with whether a person has claimed it, plus how many children you may still create. Needs a Last Price credential, and is off until child agent workspaces are switched on for your workspace.

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** read-only

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `limit` | integer | Most workspaces to return. Defaults to 50. |

## `get_partner_allowance`

Read your workspace's partner allowance: whether it is a partner (one allowed to open managed workspaces for other people's businesses), its daily allowance, how many workspaces it opened in the last 24 hours and how many remain today, how many it opened in all and how many their owners claimed. A workspace that is not a partner gets partner null and how_to_join. Only where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released). Needs a Last Price credential with partner workspaces scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, partner workspaces scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** read-only
- **REST:** `/api/partner`
- **Errors and cautions:** Only where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released).

_No arguments._

## `create_partner_workspace`

Open a managed workspace for someone's business from your partner workspace: an ordinary production workspace that can take offers, orders and customers at once, owned by an agent until the business owner claims it. The answer carries, once each and never again, your management key in the new workspace (api_key.key: full access, no expiry) and the claim link for the owner (claim.claim_url: works once, for 90 days). Keep the key and send the claim link only to the owner. Each one spends one of your daily allowance (else an error with code partner_allowance_spent). Only in a workspace Last Price staff made a partner, where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released or not_a_partner). Needs a Last Price credential with partner workspaces scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, partner workspaces scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/partner/workspaces`
- **Errors and cautions:** Each one spends one of your daily allowance (else an error with code partner_allowance_spent). Only in a workspace Last Price staff made a partner, where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released or not_a_partner).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `name` **(required)** | string | The business's name. |
| `contact_email` | string | The owner's email, if they gave one. Never used to send anything. |
| `intended_use` | string | What the business does. |

## `list_partner_workspaces`

List the workspaces your partner workspace opened for other people's businesses, newest first: each one's name, when it was opened, and whether its owner has claimed it, whether you still manage it, or whether you were let go. status narrows the list (waiting, claimed, managing, released), q searches the names, and before (the oldest opened_at you already have) pages back. Only in a workspace Last Price staff made a partner, where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released or not_a_partner). Needs a Last Price credential with partner workspaces scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, partner workspaces scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** read-only
- **REST:** `/api/partner/workspaces`
- **Errors and cautions:** Only in a workspace Last Price staff made a partner, where partner workspaces are switched on (else an error with code not_released or not_a_partner).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `status` | `all` / `waiting` / `claimed` / `managing` / `released` | Which workspaces: all (the default), waiting for their owner, claimed, still managed by you, or released. |
| `q` | string | Search the workspace names. |
| `limit` | integer | How many to return, 1 to 200 (default 50). |
| `before` | string | Only workspaces opened before this time: the oldest opened_at of the page you have. |

## `list_account_sessions`

Read the devices where you are signed in to Last Price, most recently active first: device, browser, system, approximate location, masked address, how and when each signed in, and when it was last active. Your own account, not a workspace: needs a person's sign-in token (LASTPRICE_JWT from POST /api/auth/native-token); an API key or an agent's token is refused. Answers only while recorded sessions are switched on for your account (being rolled out). Optionally pass workspace_id to include up to 100 key roots you created there and their descendants, without secrets; you must still have workspace access. This supplement is not a complete key history.

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** read-only
- **Errors and cautions:** Your own account, not a workspace: needs a person's sign-in token (LASTPRICE_JWT from POST /api/auth/native-token); an API key or an agent's token is refused.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `workspace_id` | string |  |

## `list_security_events`

Read your account's security log, newest first: sign-ins, sign-outs, devices signed out, password changes, email change requests, and API keys you created or revoked, each with when, the browser and system, and an approximate location. For older entries pass the cursor the previous answer gave as before. Your own account, not a workspace: needs a person's sign-in token (LASTPRICE_JWT from POST /api/auth/native-token); an API key or an agent's token is refused. Answers only while the security log is switched on for your account (being rolled out).

- **Access:** key
- **Behaviour:** read-only
- **Errors and cautions:** Your own account, not a workspace: needs a person's sign-in token (LASTPRICE_JWT from POST /api/auth/native-token); an API key or an agent's token is refused.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `limit` | integer | Most events to return. Defaults to 20. |
| `before` | string | The cursor the previous page returned, for older events. |

## `list_integrations`

List your workspace's integrations (Salesforce and Datadog): whether each is offered to the workspace and, when it is, its state: whether Salesforce is connected, how many records are linked and the last sync; how many Datadog key pairs are saved and the last telemetry delivery. Never a key or token. Needs a Last Price credential with the integrations:read scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, integrations:read scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** read-only

_No arguments._

## `sync_salesforce`

Run a Salesforce sync for your workspace now. direction pull reads Salesforce Accounts, Contacts and Opportunities into Last Price customers and contacts (matched by email domain or email first, created only when nothing matches); push sends each order of a linked customer to Salesforce as an Opportunity whose amount is the order total; both (the default) does both. Idempotent: a second run creates nothing new. Returns the sync log row with counts. Salesforce must be connected first, by a person in the dashboard (Settings, Integrations). Needs a Last Price credential with the integrations:write scope, and Salesforce offered to the workspace (404 otherwise; list_integrations says). Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, integrations:write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** **destructive**, reaches outside Last Price
- **Errors and cautions:** Needs a Last Price credential with the integrations:write scope, and Salesforce offered to the workspace (404 otherwise; list_integrations says).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `direction` | `pull` / `push` / `both` | What to sync. Default both. |

## `test_datadog_keys`

Check Datadog keys. With api_key, app_key and optional site (us1, us3, us5, eu1, ap1, ap2, uk1, us1_fed, us2_fed; default us1): ask Datadog whether it accepts them, saving nothing. With key_id: check a key pair saved in Settings, Integrations again and record the answer. Returns whether the pair is valid, whether each key was accepted (the application key reads null when Datadog could not check it) and the site. Needs a Last Price credential with the integrations:write scope, and Datadog offered to the workspace (404 otherwise; list_integrations says). Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, integrations:write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** reaches outside Last Price
- **Errors and cautions:** Needs a Last Price credential with the integrations:write scope, and Datadog offered to the workspace (404 otherwise; list_integrations says).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `key_id` | string | A saved key pair to check again. Give this or api_key and app_key. |
| `api_key` | string | A Datadog API key to check without saving. |
| `app_key` | string | A Datadog application key to check without saving. |
| `site` | `us1` / `us3` / `us5` / `eu1` / `ap1` / `ap2` / `uk1` / `us1_fed` / `us2_fed` | The Datadog site of the keys. Default us1. |
